title: A log that PASSES the address/topic0/to filter but carries malformed `data` (e.g. data="0x") is never tested; parseRawLogs would throw on BigInt("0x") and fail-closed, but FIND-604's malformed-data case was never actually exercised
description: parseRawLogs runs .filter() BEFORE .map() (record-earn.mjs:82-85). Test 15 (test-record-earn.sh:107-111) feeds malformed logs (wrong address/to/topic0) that are all DROPPED by the filter, so the .map() body — including Number(BigInt(l.data))/1e6 — never executes on them. There is NO test for a log that survives the filter (correct USDC address, Transfer topic0, to==founder) but whose `data` is malformed (e.g. "0x", missing, or odd-length). On the real path such a log reaches .map(), BigInt("0x") throws, externalInflow rejects, and line 119 .catch(die) fail-closes — which is the correct behavior, but it is asserted nowhere. FIND-604 fix item (3) explicitly asked for 'a malformed topic/short data asserting fail-closed (BigInt("0x") throws -> die)'; the applied tests do not cover the filter-passing variant. Not an integrity/fabrication path (fail-closed), but the only path that actually reaches the BigInt decoder with bad data is untested.
fix: Add a RAW test feeding a single log with correct address(USDC)/topic0(Transfer)/topics[2]==padded founder but data="0x" (or omitted), and assert rc!=0 AND no ledger row (fail-closed). This exercises the BigInt decoder on the only input that reaches it with bad data.
